signals.title: NZD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + ESI Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5973 anchors the G10 scorecard as the week's strongest outperformer against a broad USD decline. NZD exhibits a 1.238% average weekly gain across peers, while the USD laggard average sits at -1.233%, creating a significant 2.470% bilateral spread. This strength persists despite an accommodative NZD real rate of -1.56% and a 125bp carry disadvantage against the USD. The divergence is fundamentally supported by the Economic Surprise Index (ESI), where USD shows persistent data misses at -15.1 against a positive NZD tilt of +5.1. Technically, the pair remains firm after clearing the SMA200 at 0.5840, with the spot now trading above all major daily moving averages. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD; data divergence overrides the carry deficit. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — hold pricing dominant. Risk: Sudden hawkish repricing of Fed terminal rates closes the ESI gap and revitalizes the USD bid.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Intervention Risk + Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY is trading at 158.99, holding just below the SMA20/50 cluster at 159.67/161.01. While the 275bp Fed-BoJ carry differential remains the structural driver for USD longs, the options market is pricing in heavy protection against a move lower. The 25d risk reversal at -1.96 marks a strong put skew, indicating that institutional desks are paying a premium for downside hedges despite the carry advantage. This caution aligns with recent TIER-1 headlines regarding Treasury intervention and shifted BoJ outlooks following July CPI data. JPY COT LF net shorts at -59,526 remain crowded, though the WoW delta of +4,107 suggests initial covering as intervention fears rise. Trade bias: Neutral/Bearish USD/JPY; carry is secondary to immediate intervention and policy repricing risk. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 50% hike priced) 18 Sep — hike bias building. Risk: A clean break back above the SMA50 at 161.01 signals the carry trade has absorbed the intervention threat.

signals.title: EUR/USD — COT Extreme + Volatility Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1675, currently positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster following a 1.21% weekly gain. However, speculative positioning has reached a bearish extreme with the COT LF net short at -77,671, placing it in the 8th percentile (z -2.17) of its 52-week range. This crowded short position faces a technical squeeze as price trends higher, potentially forcing leveraged funds to cover. The options market confirms elevated uncertainty with a +2.5% Vol Risk Premium, as ATM IV at 7.1% runs well above the realized HV30 of 4.6%. The retail side is also heavily short at 80%, providing a contrarian tailwind for further upside as retail fades the institutional breakout. Trade bias: Bullish EUR/USD; extreme spec short positioning fuels a short-squeeze regime. Catalyst: Next ECB meeting 10 Sep — hike bias priced. Risk: ESI reversal or ECB dovish pivot validates the existing spec short position.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Retail Divergence + Technical Cluster
signals.text: AUD/USD is trading at 0.7166, supported by a 60bp carry advantage over the USD and a mildly restrictive real rate of +0.55%. A sharp divergence has emerged between retail sentiment and the prevailing trend, with 87% of retail traders now shorting the pair as it tests levels above the SMA200 (0.6951). This extreme retail shorting serves as a classic contrarian signal for trend continuation, especially as the pair maintains an above-cluster technical position. Speculative funds remain net long at +45,727 (75th percentile), but the absence of a COT extreme suggests there is still room for institutional long-loading. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; retail capitulation risk supports the ongoing bullish extension. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — hold pricing confirmed. Risk: Volatility spike in commodities (BCOMTR) triggers a broad-based risk-off carry unwind.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Volatility Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3625, holding comfortably above its SMA moving average cluster at 1.3391/1.3468. Despite the bullish price action and neutral 0bp carry spread vs the Fed, the options market is pricing in significant tail risk. The VRP is currently extreme at +5.1%, with 1M IV at 11.0% vs a realized HV30 of only 5.9%. This reflects the largest volatility premium in the G10 complex, suggesting traders are paying heavily for protection ahead of the September policy window. Speculative positioning is leaning long at +42,722 (90th percentile), making the pair vulnerable to a long-unwind if data begins to disappoint. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; elevated vol premium suggests the current trend is becoming expensive to hedge. Catalyst: next BoE meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) 17 Sep. Risk: A close below the SMA20 at 1.3468 triggers a liquidation of the crowded spec long.
